dedupe_keys.name: building data genome 1 electrical meter dataset

description: The first Building Data Genome dataset was assembled by Clayton Miller and Forrest Meggers to benchmark analysis of non-residential electricity demand. It contains hourly whole-building electrical meter series from 507 buildings, with one year per building and associated area, weather and use metadata. Most buildings are on university campuses, with multiple source collections, not a representative global building sample. The exact shared calendar period and geographic balance are not established in the inspected README. Public data directories and example notebooks are supplied through GitHub, whose README and repository state MIT terms. A limitation is the restricted building mix and the need to inspect measurement quality and individual source conditions before modelling. The dataset can calibrate or benchmark demand predictions used in building-energy simulations. It is distinct from Building Data Genome 2 (data-building-data-genome-2), which covers more meters, multiple energy carriers and two specified years. The original collection has its own 2017 Energy Procedia paper. No meter files or notebook datasets were downloaded.
